$comment: The dependency register: one assessment per direct dependency per manifest, against the six criteria in docs/dependency-criteria.md. Read by scripts/dependency-gate.mjs in the lockfile-review job, which fails a pull request that adds a direct dependency without an entry here, or with an entry the registry evidence contradicts; and by scripts/dependency-review.mjs, which lists open overrides and replacements every quarter. The first five entries were assessed after the fact on 27 November 2026.

maintained.why: The package is maintained (26.2.5 on 27 October 2026, four releases in the last year), but the locked 23.x line is frozen: 23.0.7 of 22 February 2024 is its last release and gets no fixes.

releasePolicy.why: Neither 23.0.7 nor the latest release carries npm provenance, and we run a major the project no longer supports; a security policy exists only in keycloak/.github.

needed.why: It is the frontend's OIDC client (packages/frontend/src/services/auth.ts: init, login, logout, token refresh) and nothing else in the tree does this; it is held at 23 to match the Keycloak 23 server, and moves with the server migration to 26.

maintained.why: One release in the last twelve months (9.0.3, 4 December 2025, after 9.0.2 in August 2023), and the recent commits are CI and release chores only: low activity for code on the token-verification path.

maintainers.why: The repository belongs to the auth0 organisation, which satisfies the signal, but a single npm account (bsmith-auth0) publishes it.

releasePolicy.why: No npm provenance, no GitHub Releases and no SECURITY.md in the repository or in auth0/.github, while four security advisories have been published against it.

footprint.why: No install script and 43 KB, but 11 of its 14 transitive packages come in only through it, seven of them single lodash.* functions.

needed.why: jose (createRemoteJWKSet with jwtVerify) does the RS256 and issuer check in auth.middleware.ts, has no dependencies, ships with provenance, and is already in the tree through jwks-rsa.

footprint.why: No install script and 6 packages only it brings, but one of them, limiter 1.1.5, has no licence recorded (#367), and 3.2.2 pulls @types/jsonwebtoken in as a runtime dependency.

needed.why: Its only use is fetching the realm's signing key in auth.middleware.ts, which jose's createRemoteJWKSet covers; jwks-rsa itself depends on jose 4, so dropping it removes a layer, not a capability.

maintained.why: No release since 9.0.10 on 16 June 2025, 17 months: the types-for-a-stable-API case, since the jsonwebtoken API they describe has not changed since 9.0.

needed.why: jsonwebtoken ships no types, and auth.middleware.ts imports GetPublicKeyOrSecret and JwtPayload from it; it goes when the move to jose (#365) removes jsonwebtoken.

maintainers.why: One npm maintainer and a repository owned by a user, not an organisation; acceptable for a dev-only runner, and ts-node, or Node's own type stripping after an import migration, is the way back.

footprint.why: It brings its own esbuild 0.28.2, which has an install script, beside the root esbuild, plus a per-platform binary, and the optional fsevents 2.3.3 (macOS only) with an install script of its own: 27 of its 28 transitive packages are only there for it, all dev-only.

needed.why: It runs the backend in development (nodemon exec tsx src/index.ts) and the TypeScript scripts; Node 24's type stripping cannot replace it while about 124 CommonJS files use extensionless relative imports.
